chunks: Hadith 4253 — Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “I guarantee for whoever mentions the Name of Allah over his food that he will not suffer from it.”

Then Ibn al-Kawwāʾ said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I ate food last night and mentioned the Name of Allah over it, then it caused me discomfort.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “You ate different kinds of food, and you mentioned the Name over some of them and did not mention it over others, O base fellow.”
And it is narrated: “Whoever forgets to mention the Name of Allah over each type, then let him say: ‘In the Name of Allah, over its beginning and its end.’”

key_terms.آذَانِي: it caused me harm or discomfort
key_terms.أَلْوَانًا: different kinds or varieties of food

ai.seo_question: What should be said if someone forgets to say Bismillah over different kinds of food?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of mentioning the Name of Allah before eating and connects that remembrance with protection from harm. It also clarifies that when a meal contains different kinds of food, the tasmiyah should cover each type, and if one forgets, one may say: “In the Name of Allah, over its beginning and its end.”

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4253 - Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:
"I guarantee that whoever mentions the name of Allah (swt) upon his food will not suffer any harm from it."

Then Ibn al-Kawwa' said:
"O Commander of the Faithful, I ate food last night, mentioned the name of Allah (swt) upon it, and yet it caused me discomfort."
Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, replied:
"You ate different types of food, but you mentioned the name of Allah (swt) on some and did not mention it on others, O foolish one!"
It is also narrated: "Whoever forgets to mention the name of Allah (swt) on each type of food should say: 'In the name of Allah (swt), on its beginning and its end.'"
